title: What Does the Bible Say About Halloween? 25 Verses
description: Should Christians celebrate Halloween? The Bible never mentions it. What it says about sorcery, darkness, light and Christian freedom, with 25 verses.
keywords: what does the bible say about halloween
summary: The Bible never mentions Halloween. The word is absent from the World English Bible and the King James Version, and the holiday is later than Scripture: it grew out of All Hallows' Eve, the night before the Christian feast of All Saints on November 1, and is often linked to the older Celtic festival of Samhain. What the Bible does speak to is the practice of the occult. Words for witchcraft, sorcery, wizards and mediums appear in 36 verses of the WEB, and Deuteronomy 18:10-12 lists divination and consulting the dead among the things Israel was to avoid. Paul also teaches that Christians have freedom in disputable matters and must act in faith and love (Romans 14, 1 Corinthians 10). Christians land in different places on Halloween, and the verses below are the ones each side uses.

faqs.a: The Bible gives no ruling on the holiday, and Christians disagree. Some avoid it because of its links to the occult and to fear of the dead, citing Deuteronomy 18:10-12 and Ephesians 5:11. Others take part in costumes and candy as harmless fun, or hold a harvest or Reformation night instead, citing Romans 14:5-6 and 1 Corinthians 10:25-27. Paul's rule for disputed questions is to be fully convinced in your own mind and to avoid making another believer stumble (Romans 14:5, 14:21).

No verse says so. What Scripture condemns is the practice of sorcery, divination and calling up the dead (Deuteronomy 18:10-12, Galatians 5:20). Whether dressing up or trick-or-treating falls under that is a judgment call, and the Bible's standard for such calls is faith, love and a clear conscience (Romans 14:23).

The name comes from All Hallows' Eve, the evening before All Saints' Day on November 1, a Christian feast. Many writers also trace the customs to the Celtic festival of Samhain, held at the start of winter. How much of the modern holiday comes from Samhain is debated among historians.

faqs.q: What does the Bible say about witchcraft?
faqs.a: It condemns it. Exodus 22:18, Deuteronomy 18:10-12, Galatians 5:19-21 and Revelation 21:8 name sorcery and divination among practices God's people are to avoid, and in Acts 19:18-19 new believers in Ephesus burned their magic books publicly.
